title: Searches rejected on some nodes
body:
Service: catalog-search. Date: 2025-01-10. Severity: SEV3.
What happened: Search requests are rejected within milliseconds on some nodes while other nodes answer normally.
Signals: the alert "catalog-search: search error rate above 20%" fired, and the logs showed "CAT-6610 request rejected: parent breaker at 96% of heap".
Root cause: A wildcard search on the description field loaded field data for the whole index into the heap of the data nodes. Heap use reached the parent circuit breaker, which rejects further requests to protect the node. The trigger was a merchandising tool that sent queries with a leading wildcard.
Resolution: Blocked leading-wildcard queries at the API, cleared the field data cache and restarted the affected nodes one at a time.

title: Signed-in users are logged out everywhere
body:
Service: auth-service. Date: 2025-02-03. Severity: SEV1.
What happened: Signed-in users are logged out and fresh logins are rejected by other services, although auth-service itself reports healthy.
Signals: the alert "auth-service: token verification failures above 30%" fired, and the logs showed "AUTH-2291 token rejected: kid=2025-q3 not in keyset".
Root cause: The signing key that auth-service used for tokens passed its expiry date and was removed from the published keyset. The service kept signing with it because the rotation job had not run, so other services rejected every token. The trigger was the quarterly rotation job having been disabled during a migration.
Resolution: Ran the key rotation by hand so that tokens were signed with a current key. Added an alert when the active key is within seven days of expiry.

title: Order placement slow for large baskets
body:
Service: checkout-api. Date: 2025-02-11. Severity: SEV1.
What happened: Order placement succeeds but takes four to five seconds, and the delay grows with the number of line items in the order.
Signals: the alert "checkout-api: PlaceOrder p99 latency above 3s" fired, and the logs showed "CHK-LAT-2210 handler=PlaceOrder p99=4800ms budget=1200ms tax_lookups=37".
Root cause: A checkout-api release replaced the batched tax calculation with one tax-service lookup per line item. The latency of PlaceOrder then grew in step with the size of the basket. The trigger was release 2025.41 of checkout-api.
Resolution: Rolled back the release and restored the batched tax call. Added a test that fails when PlaceOrder makes more than one tax lookup.

title: Ledger primary rejects all writes
body:
Service: ledger-service. Date: 2025-03-02. Severity: SEV3.
What happened: The ledger primary refuses every write at once, while reads from the replicas continue to work.
Signals: the alert "ledger-db: primary rejecting writes" fired, and the logs showed "LDG-1090 could not write to pg_wal: No space left on device".
Root cause: A replication slot for a decommissioned analytics replica was never dropped. The primary kept every WAL segment for that slot until the WAL volume was full. The trigger was the analytics replica being switched off without its slot being dropped.
Resolution: Dropped the inactive slot, which let the primary recycle WAL, and added an alert on slot lag in bytes.

title: Every email send fails immediately
body:
Service: notify-worker. Date: 2025-03-08. Severity: SEV1.
What happened: Every email send fails immediately and the workers log an error for each one, while text messages keep flowing.
Signals: the alert "notify-worker: email send failures above 90%" fired, and the logs showed "NTF-8011 lookup smtp-relay.larkhill.internal failed: SERVFAIL".
Root cause: The internal resolvers for the notify network could not answer for the larkhill.internal zone. notify-worker could not resolve the name of the SMTP relay, so it never opened a connection. The trigger was both resolvers being patched in the same maintenance window.
Resolution: Restored one resolver, staggered resolver maintenance and added a cached fallback address for the relay.

title: Checkout routes return 502 instantly
body:
Service: edge-proxy. Date: 2025-03-19. Severity: SEV1.
What happened: All checkout routes return 502 within milliseconds, although the checkout pods are healthy and reachable by address.
Signals: the alert "edge-proxy: 502 rate above 50% on checkout routes" fired, and the logs showed "EDG-9140 upstream resolve failed host=checkout.larkhill.internal NXDOMAIN".
Root cause: The internal DNS record for checkout.larkhill.internal was deleted when its service entry was recreated under a new name. edge-proxy could not resolve its upstream, so it had nowhere to send checkout requests. The trigger was a service rename that removed the old record before the proxy was pointed at the new one.
Resolution: Recreated the record as an alias of the new name and updated the proxy's upstream. Added a check that a record is unreferenced before it is deleted.

title: Card authorisations declined in bursts
body:
Service: payments-gateway. Date: 2025-04-05. Severity: SEV2.
What happened: Card authorisations are declined in bursts while traffic is high, and the same card often succeeds on a retry a minute later.
Signals: the alert "payments-gateway: authorisation decline rate above 8%" fired, and the logs showed "PGW-4012 authorisation declined by upstream code=R29 route=acq-primary".
Root cause: Meridian Acquiring limits our merchant account to 300 authorisations per second. It answers traffic above that limit with R29 declines, which the gateway logs as PGW-4012. The trigger was a flash sale that pushed the peak to 420 authorisations per second.
Resolution: Enabled the gateway's outbound limiter at 280 per second with queueing, and asked Meridian for a higher limit.

title: Stock reservations fail during the afternoon import
body:
Service: inventory-sync. Date: 2025-04-14. Severity: SEV3.
What happened: Stock reservations fail now and then during the afternoon bulk import and succeed when retried.
Signals: the alert "inventory-sync: reservation failures above 5%" fired, and the logs showed "INV-5207 deadlock detected: reserve_stock chosen as victim".
Root cause: The bulk stock import updates rows in file order while reservations lock rows in basket order. When both touch the same two products in opposite order, the database detects a deadlock and aborts the reservation. The trigger was the daily supplier import overlapping the afternoon sales peak.
Resolution: Made the import sort its rows by product id, the order that reservations use, and made a reservation retry once after a deadlock.

title: Product updates rejected, search results stale
body:
Service: catalog-search. Date: 2025-05-15. Severity: SEV1.
What happened: Product updates are rejected, so the prices and stock shown in search go stale, while searching itself keeps working.
Signals: the alert "catalog-search: indexing failures above 100 per minute" fired, and the logs showed "CAT-6120 write blocked: index read-only FORBIDDEN/12".
Root cause: The data nodes passed the flood-stage disk watermark of 95%. The search cluster then marked every index read-only, which rejects all writes. The trigger was old daily indices that the retention job had stopped deleting.
Resolution: Deleted the indices that were no longer needed and cleared the read-only block. Added an alert at 85% disk use.

title: Ledger writes fail shortly after 02:00 UTC
body:
Service: ledger-service. Date: 2025-06-20. Severity: SEV1.
What happened: Ledger writes fail for ten to fifteen minutes shortly after 02:00 UTC and then recover without any action.
Signals: the alert "ledger-service: write error rate above 10%" fired, and the logs showed "LDG-7741 statement cancelled after 5000ms wait rel=settlements pid=48213".
Root cause: The nightly settle-batch job takes an exclusive lock on the settlements table while it rewrites the day's rows. Ledger writes wait for that lock and are cancelled at the five-second lock timeout. The trigger was month-end volume that stretched the job from two minutes to fourteen.
Resolution: Changed settle-batch to work in batches of 5,000 rows under row-level locks, so writers are no longer blocked.

title: Captures time out while authorisations stay fast
body:
Service: payments-gateway. Date: 2025-07-21. Severity: SEV3.
What happened: Captures time out after ten seconds while authorisations, which do not write to the ledger, stay fast.
Signals: the alert "payments-gateway: capture latency p99 above 8s" fired, and the logs showed "PGW-3301 no backend slot for ledger write cl_waiting=180".
Root cause: The ledger connection pooler gives payments-gateway 60 server connections. Transactions held open on the capture path used all 60, and new captures queued for a slot until they timed out. The trigger was a capture retry job that opened a transaction for each retry and held it across the acquirer call.
Resolution: Raised the pooler limit to 120 and moved the acquirer call outside the ledger transaction, so that a capture holds its connection only briefly.

title: Thousands of products drop to zero stock
body:
Service: inventory-sync. Date: 2025-08-12. Severity: SEV1.
What happened: Thousands of products from one warehouse drop to zero stock at once, while the warehouse reports normal levels.
Signals: the alert "inventory-sync: skipped feed rows above 1000" fired, and the logs showed "INV-5611 unmapped location code count=4312 feed=warehouse-north".
Root cause: The location mapping table, which translates warehouse location codes into site regions, was edited, and the rows for the northern warehouse were replaced with a new code format. Feed rows with the old codes no longer matched and were skipped, which the site reads as zero stock. The trigger was a mapping update prepared for a warehouse system upgrade that had not gone live.
Resolution: Restored the previous mapping rows from the config history and ran the feed again.

title: Login loops on Safari
body:
Service: auth-service. Date: 2025-08-15. Severity: SEV3.
What happened: Logins loop back to the login page for users on Safari, while other browsers sign in normally.
Signals: the alert "auth-service: login completion rate below 70%" fired, and the logs showed "AUTH-2317 callback without session cookie agent=Safari".
Root cause: An auth-service release changed the session cookie to SameSite=None without the Secure attribute. Safari drops such cookies, so the login callback arrived without a session and redirected back to the login page. The trigger was release 2025.38 of auth-service, which upgraded the web framework and with it the cookie defaults.
Resolution: Rolled back the release and set the cookie attributes explicitly, with a browser test that covers Safari.

title: Browsers show a security warning for the shop
body:
Service: edge-proxy. Date: 2025-08-15. Severity: SEV2.
What happened: Browsers show a security warning for the shop and the apps fail to connect, while internal health checks over plain HTTP still pass.
Signals: the alert "edge-proxy: successful TLS handshakes at zero" fired, and the logs showed "EDG-9001 tls handshake aborted sni=shop.larkhill.example alert=45".
Root cause: The public certificate for shop.larkhill.example passed its expiry date. The renewal client had stopped running, and nothing alerted on the approaching expiry. The trigger was the renewal timer not having been enabled again after a host migration.
Resolution: Issued a new certificate, reloaded the proxies and repaired the renewal client. Added an alert when a certificate has under 14 days left.

title: Adding to the basket fails with 503
body:
Service: checkout-api. Date: 2025-08-20. Severity: SEV2.
What happened: Adding items to the basket fails with 503 after a three-second wait, while orders for baskets that already exist are still placed.
Signals: the alert "checkout-api: 503 rate above 2% on /v1/cart" fired, and the logs showed "CHK-POOL-0417 cart-cache connection acquire timed out after 3000ms active=40 idle=0 waiting=212".
Root cause: After a cart-cache failover, checkout-api kept half-open connections to the old primary in its pool. The pool of 40 never evicted them, so every request waited for a connection until the acquire timeout. The trigger was a planned cart-cache failover during maintenance.
Resolution: Restarted the checkout-api pods to rebuild the pool, then enabled connection validation on borrow.

title: Paid orders stuck in review
body:
Service: checkout-api. Date: 2025-09-13. Severity: SEV3.
What happened: New orders are accepted and paid but stay in PENDING_REVIEW and never reach CONFIRMED, so customers get no confirmation.
Signals: the alert "checkout-api: orders pending review above 500" fired, and the logs showed "CHK-ORD-3306 order held in PENDING_REVIEW for more than 120s reason=fraud_async".
Root cause: The feature flag checkout.async_fraud_check was switched on in the production flag set. With the flag on, an order waits for a fraud-review callback that no service sends yet. The trigger was a flag change that was meant for the staging flag set.
Resolution: Switched the flag off and replayed the held orders through the synchronous fraud check.

title: Common searches return nothing
body:
Service: catalog-search. Date: 2025-09-25. Severity: SEV2.
What happened: Searches answer quickly with zero results for common terms, and no error is shown to users.
Signals: the alert "catalog-search: zero-result rate above 40%" fired, and the logs showed "CAT-6405 analyzer reload failed set=synonyms_v41 line=2207".
Root cause: A new synonym set was published with a malformed rule. The analyzer failed to reload on the search nodes, and queries that pass through the synonym filter matched nothing. The trigger was synonym set v41, which had an unclosed bracket on one line.
Resolution: Reverted to the previous synonym set and reloaded the analyzers. Added validation to the synonym publish step.

title: Text messages delayed or never sent
body:
Service: notify-worker. Date: 2025-09-28. Severity: SEV2.
What happened: Text messages are delayed by many minutes or never sent, while emails go out normally.
Signals: the alert "notify-worker: SMS delivery rate below 50%" fired, and the logs showed "NTF-8450 provider answered 429 bucket=sms-tx retry_after=60".
Root cause: Tessel SMS caps our account at 50 messages per second. A bulk send went out through the transactional sender and used the whole allowance, so one-time codes were throttled with 429 responses. The trigger was a marketing campaign of 200,000 texts sent through the transactional sender.
Resolution: Paused the bulk send, moved bulk messages to their own sender with a separate cap and gave one-time codes priority in the queue.

title: Logins time out, existing sessions keep working
body:
Service: auth-service. Date: 2025-09-29. Severity: SEV3.
What happened: Logins and sign-ups time out after five seconds, while the verification of existing tokens stays fast.
Signals: the alert "auth-service: login latency p99 above 5s" fired, and the logs showed "AUTH-2105 user-db pool exhausted: 30 of 30 in use, 96 waiting".
Root cause: auth-service rehashes a password at login when the stored hash uses the old algorithm, and it holds a user-db connection for the whole rehash. With 30 connections in the pool, a peak of logins by users with old hashes used them all, and further logins waited until they timed out. The trigger was the Monday morning login peak.
Resolution: Moved the rehash to a background queue so that a login holds its connection for milliseconds, and raised the pool to 60.

title: ledger-service pods restart during statement exports
body:
Service: ledger-service. Date: 2025-10-26. Severity: SEV1.
What happened: ledger-service pods restart every few minutes, and requests in flight on a restarted pod fail.
Signals: the alert "ledger-service: pod restarts above 5 in 10 minutes" fired, and the logs showed "LDG-2203 worker exited signal=9 rss=7.8G limit=8G task=statement-export".
Root cause: The statement export loads a merchant's full history into memory before it writes the file. For the largest merchants this exceeds the pod's 8 GB limit and the kernel kills the worker. The trigger was a year-end export for the largest merchant.
Resolution: Changed the export to stream rows with a server-side cursor and capped the date range of one request.

title: Every card authorisation fails at once
body:
Service: payments-gateway. Date: 2025-11-04. Severity: SEV2.
What happened: Every card authorisation fails within milliseconds and no request reaches the acquirer.
Signals: the alert "payments-gateway: authorisation success rate below 5%" fired, and the logs showed "PGW-5120 handshake with acq-primary failed alert=45".
Root cause: The client certificate that payments-gateway presents to Meridian Acquiring for mutual TLS passed its expiry date. Meridian rejected the handshake with alert 45, so no authorisation could be sent. The trigger was the yearly certificate expiring at 00:00 UTC while the renewal ticket was still open.
Resolution: Deployed the renewed client certificate and restarted the gateway's outbound connectors. Added an alert 30 days before expiry.

title: Stock levels hours behind the warehouses
body:
Service: inventory-sync. Date: 2025-11-04. Severity: SEV3.
What happened: Stock levels on the site fall hours behind the warehouses, so items show as available after they have sold out.
Signals: the alert "inventory-sync: stock-apply lag above 100000" fired, and the logs showed "INV-5530 consumer lag=184000 partition=7 group=stock-apply".
Root cause: Stock events are partitioned by warehouse, and one warehouse produced far more events than the rest. Its partition has a single consumer, which could not keep up, so that warehouse's stock updates queued for hours. The trigger was a full stock recount at the largest warehouse.
Resolution: Repartitioned stock events by product so that load spreads evenly, and added consumers to the group.

title: Signed-in users get an error on every page
body:
Service: edge-proxy. Date: 2025-11-10. Severity: SEV2.
What happened: Some signed-in users get an error page on every request, while signed-out visitors browse normally.
Signals: the alert "edge-proxy: 431 responses above 1%" fired, and the logs showed "EDG-9212 request rejected status=431 header_bytes=9120 limit=8192".
Root cause: An edge-proxy release lowered the maximum size of request headers from 16 KB to 8 KB, the default of the upgraded proxy library. Users with many cookies sent larger headers and were rejected with 431. The trigger was release 2025.44 of edge-proxy, which upgraded the proxy library.
Resolution: Rolled back the release and set the header limit explicitly to 16 KB, with a test that sends a 12 KB header.

title: Transactional emails stop while workers look healthy
body:
Service: notify-worker. Date: 2025-11-13. Severity: SEV2.
What happened: Transactional emails stop going out and the email queue grows, while the workers stay up and report healthy.
Signals: the alert "notify-worker: email-tx queue depth above 20000" fired, and the logs showed "NTF-8102 message returned to queue redelivery=57 queue=email-tx".
Root cause: One message referred to an attachment that no longer existed, which made the worker throw before it acknowledged the message. The broker redelivered that message to every worker in turn, and the queue stalled behind it. The trigger was a receipt whose PDF had been removed by a storage clean-up before the email was sent.
Resolution: Moved the message to the dead-letter queue by hand and set a redelivery limit of five, so the broker does it automatically.

Signals: the alert "catalog-search: search error rate above 20%" fired, and the logs showed "CAT-6610 request rejected: parent breaker at 96% of heap".
Root cause: A wildcard search on the description field loaded field data for the whole index into the heap of the data nodes. Heap use reached the parent circuit breaker, which rejects further requests to protect the node. The trigger was a crawler that hit the search endpoint with wildcard terms.
Resolution: Blocked leading-wildcard queries at the API, cleared the field data cache and restarted the affected nodes one at a time.

title: Repeat of INC-2025-0114: Every email send fails immediately
body:
Service: notify-worker. Date: 2026-06-27. Severity: SEV1.
What happened: The same pattern as INC-2025-0114. Every email send fails immediately and the workers log an error for each one, while text messages keep flowing.
Signals: the alert "notify-worker: email send failures above 90%" fired, and the logs showed "NTF-8011 lookup smtp-relay.larkhill.internal failed: SERVFAIL".
Root cause: The internal resolvers for the notify network could not answer for the larkhill.internal zone. notify-worker could not resolve the name of the SMTP relay, so it never opened a connection. The trigger was a resolver that lost its forwarder after a restart.
Resolution: Restored one resolver, staggered resolver maintenance and added a cached fallback address for the relay.

title: Repeat of INC-2025-0388: Common searches return nothing
body:
Service: catalog-search. Date: 2026-07-29. Severity: SEV3.
What happened: The same pattern as INC-2025-0388. Searches answer quickly with zero results for common terms, and no error is shown to users.
Signals: the alert "catalog-search: zero-result rate above 40%" fired, and the logs showed "CAT-6405 analyzer reload failed set=synonyms_v41 line=2207".
Root cause: A new synonym set was published with a malformed rule. The analyzer failed to reload on the search nodes, and queries that pass through the synonym filter matched nothing. The trigger was a synonym export from the merchandising tool that used the wrong delimiter.
Resolution: Reverted to the previous synonym set and reloaded the analyzers. Added validation to the synonym publish step.

title: Repeat of INC-2025-0434: Logins time out, existing sessions keep working
body:
Service: auth-service. Date: 2026-08-04. Severity: SEV3.
What happened: The same pattern as INC-2025-0434. Logins and sign-ups time out after five seconds, while the verification of existing tokens stays fast.
Signals: the alert "auth-service: login latency p99 above 5s" fired, and the logs showed "AUTH-2105 user-db pool exhausted: 30 of 30 in use, 96 waiting".
Root cause: auth-service rehashes a password at login when the stored hash uses the old algorithm, and it holds a user-db connection for the whole rehash. With 30 connections in the pool, a peak of logins by users with old hashes used them all, and further logins waited until they timed out. The trigger was an email campaign that sent many dormant users to log in at once.
Resolution: Moved the rehash to a background queue so that a login holds its connection for milliseconds, and raised the pool to 60.

title: Repeat of INC-2025-0489: Every card authorisation fails at once
body:
Service: payments-gateway. Date: 2026-08-18. Severity: SEV3.
What happened: The same pattern as INC-2025-0489. Every card authorisation fails within milliseconds and no request reaches the acquirer.
Signals: the alert "payments-gateway: authorisation success rate below 5%" fired, and the logs showed "PGW-5120 handshake with acq-primary failed alert=45".
Root cause: The client certificate that payments-gateway presents to Meridian Acquiring for mutual TLS passed its expiry date. Meridian rejected the handshake with alert 45, so no authorisation could be sent. The trigger was a renewed certificate that had been issued but never deployed to the gateway.
Resolution: Deployed the renewed client certificate and restarted the gateway's outbound connectors. Added an alert 30 days before expiry.

title: Repeat of INC-2025-0206: Product updates rejected, search results stale
body:
Service: catalog-search. Date: 2026-08-18. Severity: SEV1.
What happened: The same pattern as INC-2025-0206. Product updates are rejected, so the prices and stock shown in search go stale, while searching itself keeps working.
Signals: the alert "catalog-search: indexing failures above 100 per minute" fired, and the logs showed "CAT-6120 write blocked: index read-only FORBIDDEN/12".
Root cause: The data nodes passed the flood-stage disk watermark of 95%. The search cluster then marked every index read-only, which rejects all writes. The trigger was a full reindex that doubled disk use while both copies existed.
Resolution: Deleted the indices that were no longer needed and cleared the read-only block. Added an alert at 85% disk use.

title: Repeat of INC-2025-0417: Text messages delayed or never sent
body:
Service: notify-worker. Date: 2026-08-20. Severity: SEV2.
What happened: The same pattern as INC-2025-0417. Text messages are delayed by many minutes or never sent, while emails go out normally.
Signals: the alert "notify-worker: SMS delivery rate below 50%" fired, and the logs showed "NTF-8450 provider answered 429 bucket=sms-tx retry_after=60".
Root cause: Tessel SMS caps our account at 50 messages per second. A bulk send went out through the transactional sender and used the whole allowance, so one-time codes were throttled with 429 responses. The trigger was a loop that resent delivery texts for a whole afternoon.
Resolution: Paused the bulk send, moved bulk messages to their own sender with a separate cap and gave one-time codes priority in the queue.

title: Repeat of INC-2025-0552: Transactional emails stop while workers look healthy
body:
Service: notify-worker. Date: 2026-08-22. Severity: SEV1.
What happened: The same pattern as INC-2025-0552. Transactional emails stop going out and the email queue grows, while the workers stay up and report healthy.
Signals: the alert "notify-worker: email-tx queue depth above 20000" fired, and the logs showed "NTF-8102 message returned to queue redelivery=57 queue=email-tx".
Root cause: One message referred to an attachment that no longer existed, which made the worker throw before it acknowledged the message. The broker redelivered that message to every worker in turn, and the queue stalled behind it. The trigger was a message that pointed at an attachment in a bucket that had been emptied.
Resolution: Moved the message to the dead-letter queue by hand and set a redelivery limit of five, so the broker does it automatically.

title: Repeat of INC-2025-0103: Ledger primary rejects all writes
body:
Service: ledger-service. Date: 2026-08-23. Severity: SEV1.
What happened: The same pattern as INC-2025-0103. The ledger primary refuses every write at once, while reads from the replicas continue to work.
Signals: the alert "ledger-db: primary rejecting writes" fired, and the logs showed "LDG-1090 could not write to pg_wal: No space left on device".
Root cause: A replication slot for a decommissioned analytics replica was never dropped. The primary kept every WAL segment for that slot until the WAL volume was full. The trigger was a logical replication slot left behind by a migration rehearsal.
Resolution: Dropped the inactive slot, which let the primary recycle WAL, and added an alert on slot lag in bytes.

title: Repeat of INC-2025-0251: Captures time out while authorisations stay fast
body:
Service: payments-gateway. Date: 2026-09-12. Severity: SEV2.
What happened: The same pattern as INC-2025-0251. Captures time out after ten seconds while authorisations, which do not write to the ledger, stay fast.
Signals: the alert "payments-gateway: capture latency p99 above 8s" fired, and the logs showed "PGW-3301 no backend slot for ledger write cl_waiting=180".
Root cause: The ledger connection pooler gives payments-gateway 60 server connections. Transactions held open on the capture path used all 60, and new captures queued for a slot until they timed out. The trigger was a traffic peak while the pooler was still at its old limit of 60.
Resolution: Raised the pooler limit to 120 and moved the acquirer call outside the ledger transaction, so that a capture holds its connection only briefly.

title: Repeat of INC-2025-0319: Browsers show a security warning for the shop
body:
Service: edge-proxy. Date: 2026-09-19. Severity: SEV3.
What happened: The same pattern as INC-2025-0319. Browsers show a security warning for the shop and the apps fail to connect, while internal health checks over plain HTTP still pass.
Signals: the alert "edge-proxy: successful TLS handshakes at zero" fired, and the logs showed "EDG-9001 tls handshake aborted sni=shop.larkhill.example alert=45".
Root cause: The public certificate for shop.larkhill.example passed its expiry date. The renewal client had stopped running, and nothing alerted on the approaching expiry. The trigger was the renewal client crashing at start-up since an operating system upgrade.
Resolution: Issued a new certificate, reloaded the proxies and repaired the renewal client. Added an alert when a certificate has under 14 days left.

title: auth-service: overview and escalation
body: auth-service handles login, registration and session tokens. It stores users in user-db and publishes the keyset that other services use to verify tokens. The identity on-call owns it. Dashboards: 'Login funnel' and 'Token verification'.

title: Signed-in users are logged out everywhere
body:
Applies to: auth-service.
Use this section when: Signed-in users are logged out and fresh logins are rejected by other services, although auth-service itself reports healthy.
Signals: the alert "auth-service: token verification failures above 30%", and log lines such as "AUTH-2291 token rejected: kid=2025-q3 not in keyset".
Why it happens: The signing key that auth-service used for tokens passed its expiry date and was removed from the published keyset. The service kept signing with it because the rotation job had not run, so other services rejected every token.
Steps:
1. Compare the kid in AUTH-2291 lines with the keys in the published keyset.
2. Check when the key rotation job last succeeded.
3. Run the rotation by hand and confirm that new tokens verify.

title: Login loops on Safari
body:
Applies to: auth-service.
Use this section when: Logins loop back to the login page for users on Safari, while other browsers sign in normally.
Signals: the alert "auth-service: login completion rate below 70%", and log lines such as "AUTH-2317 callback without session cookie agent=Safari".
Why it happens: An auth-service release changed the session cookie to SameSite=None without the Secure attribute. Safari drops such cookies, so the login callback arrived without a session and redirected back to the login page.
Steps:
1. Group AUTH-2317 lines by agent: Safari alone confirms the cookie problem.
2. Check the deploy log for an auth-service release in the last day.
3. Roll back the release.

title: Logins time out, existing sessions keep working
body:
Applies to: auth-service.
Use this section when: Logins and sign-ups time out after five seconds, while the verification of existing tokens stays fast.
Signals: the alert "auth-service: login latency p99 above 5s", and log lines such as "AUTH-2105 user-db pool exhausted: 30 of 30 in use, 96 waiting".
Why it happens: auth-service rehashes a password at login when the stored hash uses the old algorithm, and it holds a user-db connection for the whole rehash. With 30 connections in the pool, a peak of logins by users with old hashes used them all, and further logins waited until they timed out.
Steps:
1. Check the user-db pool gauge on 'Login funnel' for 30 of 30 in use.
2. Look for connections held for seconds by the login handler.
3. Switch off the in-request rehash to release connections.

title: catalog-search: overview and escalation
body: catalog-search serves product search from a search cluster of three data nodes. inventory-sync and the merchandising tool write product updates into it. The discovery on-call owns it. Dashboards: 'Search traffic' and 'Search cluster health'.

title: Searches rejected on some nodes
body:
Applies to: catalog-search.
Use this section when: Search requests are rejected within milliseconds on some nodes while other nodes answer normally.
Signals: the alert "catalog-search: search error rate above 20%", and log lines such as "CAT-6610 request rejected: parent breaker at 96% of heap".
Why it happens: A wildcard search on the description field loaded field data for the whole index into the heap of the data nodes. Heap use reached the parent circuit breaker, which rejects further requests to protect the node.
Steps:
1. Check heap use per node on 'Search cluster health': the nodes above 90% are the ones that reject.
2. Look in the slow log for wildcard queries on the description field.
3. Clear the field data cache, then block the source of the queries.

title: Product updates rejected, search results stale
body:
Applies to: catalog-search.
Use this section when: Product updates are rejected, so the prices and stock shown in search go stale, while searching itself keeps working.
Signals: the alert "catalog-search: indexing failures above 100 per minute", and log lines such as "CAT-6120 write blocked: index read-only FORBIDDEN/12".
Why it happens: The data nodes passed the flood-stage disk watermark of 95%. The search cluster then marked every index read-only, which rejects all writes.
Steps:
1. Check disk use on the data nodes against the flood-stage watermark of 95%.
2. List the indices by size and age to find what can be deleted.
3. Free space, then remove the read-only block from the indices.

title: Common searches return nothing
body:
Applies to: catalog-search.
Use this section when: Searches answer quickly with zero results for common terms, and no error is shown to users.
Signals: the alert "catalog-search: zero-result rate above 40%", and log lines such as "CAT-6405 analyzer reload failed set=synonyms_v41 line=2207".
Why it happens: A new synonym set was published with a malformed rule. The analyzer failed to reload on the search nodes, and queries that pass through the synonym filter matched nothing.
Steps:
1. Find CAT-6405 lines to see which synonym set failed and on which line.
2. Check the config history for a synonym publish in the last day.
3. Revert to the previous set and reload the analyzers.

title: checkout-api: overview and escalation
body: checkout-api holds baskets and places orders. It calls cart-cache for basket state, payments-gateway for card payments, inventory-sync for stock reservations and the tax service for tax. The checkout on-call owns it. Dashboards: 'Checkout overview' and 'Checkout dependencies'.

title: Adding to the basket fails with 503
body:
Applies to: checkout-api.
Use this section when: Adding items to the basket fails with 503 after a three-second wait, while orders for baskets that already exist are still placed.
Signals: the alert "checkout-api: 503 rate above 2% on /v1/cart", and log lines such as "CHK-POOL-0417 cart-cache connection acquire timed out after 3000ms active=40 idle=0 waiting=212".
Why it happens: After a cart-cache failover, checkout-api kept half-open connections to the old primary in its pool. The pool of 40 never evicted them, so every request waited for a connection until the acquire timeout.
Steps:
1. Check the pool gauges on 'Checkout dependencies': active at 40 with idle at 0 confirms exhaustion.
2. Look for a cart-cache failover or restart in the last hour.
3. Restart the checkout-api pods one zone at a time to rebuild the pool.

title: Order placement slow for large baskets
body:
Applies to: checkout-api.
Use this section when: Order placement succeeds but takes four to five seconds, and the delay grows with the number of line items in the order.
Signals: the alert "checkout-api: PlaceOrder p99 latency above 3s", and log lines such as "CHK-LAT-2210 handler=PlaceOrder p99=4800ms budget=1200ms tax_lookups=37".
Why it happens: A checkout-api release replaced the batched tax calculation with one tax-service lookup per line item. The latency of PlaceOrder then grew in step with the size of the basket.
Steps:
1. Compare the tax_lookups field in CHK-LAT-2210 lines with the number of line items: one lookup per item confirms the regression.
2. Check the deploy log for a checkout-api release in the last day.
3. Roll back to the previous release.

title: Paid orders stuck in review
body:
Applies to: checkout-api.
Use this section when: New orders are accepted and paid but stay in PENDING_REVIEW and never reach CONFIRMED, so customers get no confirmation.
Signals: the alert "checkout-api: orders pending review above 500", and log lines such as "CHK-ORD-3306 order held in PENDING_REVIEW for more than 120s reason=fraud_async".
Why it happens: The feature flag checkout.async_fraud_check was switched on in the production flag set. With the flag on, an order waits for a fraud-review callback that no service sends yet.
Steps:
1. Read the current value of checkout.async_fraud_check in the production flag set.
2. Check the flag audit log for a change in the last day.
3. Switch the flag off, then run the replay job for orders in PENDING_REVIEW.

title: edge-proxy: overview and escalation
body: edge-proxy terminates TLS for shop.larkhill.example and routes requests to the internal services by path. The platform on-call owns it. Dashboards: 'Edge traffic' and 'Edge TLS'.

title: Browsers show a security warning for the shop
body:
Applies to: edge-proxy.
Use this section when: Browsers show a security warning for the shop and the apps fail to connect, while internal health checks over plain HTTP still pass.
Signals: the alert "edge-proxy: successful TLS handshakes at zero", and log lines such as "EDG-9001 tls handshake aborted sni=shop.larkhill.example alert=45".
Why it happens: The public certificate for shop.larkhill.example passed its expiry date. The renewal client had stopped running, and nothing alerted on the approaching expiry.
Steps:
1. Read the notAfter date of the certificate served on port 443.
2. Check when the renewal client last ran successfully.
3. Issue a new certificate and reload the edge proxies.

title: Checkout routes return 502 instantly
body:
Applies to: edge-proxy.
Use this section when: All checkout routes return 502 within milliseconds, although the checkout pods are healthy and reachable by address.
Signals: the alert "edge-proxy: 502 rate above 50% on checkout routes", and log lines such as "EDG-9140 upstream resolve failed host=checkout.larkhill.internal NXDOMAIN".
Why it happens: The internal DNS record for checkout.larkhill.internal was deleted when its service entry was recreated under a new name. edge-proxy could not resolve its upstream, so it had nowhere to send checkout requests.
Steps:
1. Resolve checkout.larkhill.internal from an edge-proxy host.
2. Check the DNS change log for a deletion in the internal zone.
3. Recreate the record or point the upstream at the new name.

title: Signed-in users get an error on every page
body:
Applies to: edge-proxy.
Use this section when: Some signed-in users get an error page on every request, while signed-out visitors browse normally.
Signals: the alert "edge-proxy: 431 responses above 1%", and log lines such as "EDG-9212 request rejected status=431 header_bytes=9120 limit=8192".
Why it happens: An edge-proxy release lowered the maximum size of request headers from 16 KB to 8 KB, the default of the upgraded proxy library. Users with many cookies sent larger headers and were rejected with 431.
Steps:
1. Compare header_bytes with limit in EDG-9212 lines: requests just above 8192 confirm the lowered limit.
2. Check the deploy log for an edge-proxy release in the last day.
3. Roll back the release.

title: inventory-sync: overview and escalation
body: inventory-sync applies stock events from the warehouses, takes stock reservations from checkout-api and pushes stock levels to catalog-search. The supply on-call owns it. Dashboards: 'Stock pipeline' and 'Reservations'.

title: Stock levels hours behind the warehouses
body:
Applies to: inventory-sync.
Use this section when: Stock levels on the site fall hours behind the warehouses, so items show as available after they have sold out.
Signals: the alert "inventory-sync: stock-apply lag above 100000", and log lines such as "INV-5530 consumer lag=184000 partition=7 group=stock-apply".
Why it happens: Stock events are partitioned by warehouse, and one warehouse produced far more events than the rest. Its partition has a single consumer, which could not keep up, so that warehouse's stock updates queued for hours.
Steps:
1. Check the lag per partition for the stock-apply group: one partition far ahead of the rest confirms a hot partition.
2. Identify which warehouse maps to that partition and what it is sending.
3. Add a temporary consumer for the hot partition or pause the resend.

title: Stock reservations fail during the afternoon import
body:
Applies to: inventory-sync.
Use this section when: Stock reservations fail now and then during the afternoon bulk import and succeed when retried.
Signals: the alert "inventory-sync: reservation failures above 5%", and log lines such as "INV-5207 deadlock detected: reserve_stock chosen as victim".
Why it happens: The bulk stock import updates rows in file order while reservations lock rows in basket order. When both touch the same two products in opposite order, the database detects a deadlock and aborts the reservation.
Steps:
1. Count INV-5207 lines and check that they fall inside the import window.
2. Confirm in the database log that the other transaction in each deadlock is the bulk import.
3. Pause the import until the peak has passed.

title: Thousands of products drop to zero stock
body:
Applies to: inventory-sync.
Use this section when: Thousands of products from one warehouse drop to zero stock at once, while the warehouse reports normal levels.
Signals: the alert "inventory-sync: skipped feed rows above 1000", and log lines such as "INV-5611 unmapped location code count=4312 feed=warehouse-north".
Why it happens: The location mapping table, which translates warehouse location codes into site regions, was edited, and the rows for the northern warehouse were replaced with a new code format. Feed rows with the old codes no longer matched and were skipped, which the site reads as zero stock.
Steps:
1. Check INV-5611 lines for the feed name and the count of unmapped codes.
2. Compare the location mapping table with its previous version in the config history.
3. Restore the previous mapping and run the feed again.

title: ledger-service: overview and escalation
body: ledger-service is the API in front of ledger-db, the PostgreSQL cluster that holds the ledger. One primary takes writes and two replicas serve reads. The ledger on-call owns the service and the database. Dashboards: 'Ledger writes' and 'Ledger database'.

title: Ledger writes fail shortly after 02:00 UTC
body:
Applies to: ledger-service.
Use this section when: Ledger writes fail for ten to fifteen minutes shortly after 02:00 UTC and then recover without any action.
Signals: the alert "ledger-service: write error rate above 10%", and log lines such as "LDG-7741 statement cancelled after 5000ms wait rel=settlements pid=48213".
Why it happens: The nightly settle-batch job takes an exclusive lock on the settlements table while it rewrites the day's rows. Ledger writes wait for that lock and are cancelled at the five-second lock timeout.
Steps:
1. Query pg_locks for an AccessExclusiveLock on settlements and note the pid that holds it.
2. Check whether settle-batch is running and for how long.
3. If writes must recover now, cancel the job's backend. The job is safe to rerun.

title: Ledger primary rejects all writes
body:
Applies to: ledger-service.
Use this section when: The ledger primary refuses every write at once, while reads from the replicas continue to work.
Signals: the alert "ledger-db: primary rejecting writes", and log lines such as "LDG-1090 could not write to pg_wal: No space left on device".
Why it happens: A replication slot for a decommissioned analytics replica was never dropped. The primary kept every WAL segment for that slot until the WAL volume was full.
Steps:
1. Check the free space on the WAL volume of the primary.
2. Query pg_replication_slots for inactive slots with a large lag behind the current WAL position.
3. Drop the inactive slot after confirming that nothing consumes it.

title: ledger-service pods restart during statement exports
body:
Applies to: ledger-service.
Use this section when: ledger-service pods restart every few minutes, and requests in flight on a restarted pod fail.
Signals: the alert "ledger-service: pod restarts above 5 in 10 minutes", and log lines such as "LDG-2203 worker exited signal=9 rss=7.8G limit=8G task=statement-export".
Why it happens: The statement export loads a merchant's full history into memory before it writes the file. For the largest merchants this exceeds the pod's 8 GB limit and the kernel kills the worker.
Steps:
1. Check the last termination reason of the restarted pods: OOMKilled confirms it.
2. Find the task named in LDG-2203 lines and who requested it.
3. Cancel the export and ask for a smaller date range.

title: notify-worker: overview and escalation
body: notify-worker sends transactional email through the internal SMTP relay and text messages through Tessel SMS. Other services queue messages on email-tx and sms-tx. The messaging on-call owns it. Dashboard: 'Notification queues'.

title: Transactional emails stop while workers look healthy
body:
Applies to: notify-worker.
Use this section when: Transactional emails stop going out and the email queue grows, while the workers stay up and report healthy.
Signals: the alert "notify-worker: email-tx queue depth above 20000", and log lines such as "NTF-8102 message returned to queue redelivery=57 queue=email-tx".
Why it happens: One message referred to an attachment that no longer existed, which made the worker throw before it acknowledged the message. The broker redelivered that message to every worker in turn, and the queue stalled behind it.
Steps:
1. Look for NTF-8102 lines with a high redelivery count: they name the stuck message.
2. Check on 'Notification queues' that the workers consume but do not acknowledge.
3. Move the stuck message to the dead-letter queue.

title: Text messages delayed or never sent
body:
Applies to: notify-worker.
Use this section when: Text messages are delayed by many minutes or never sent, while emails go out normally.
Signals: the alert "notify-worker: SMS delivery rate below 50%", and log lines such as "NTF-8450 provider answered 429 bucket=sms-tx retry_after=60".
Why it happens: Tessel SMS caps our account at 50 messages per second. A bulk send went out through the transactional sender and used the whole allowance, so one-time codes were throttled with 429 responses.
Steps:
1. Compare the SMS send rate with the cap of 50 per second on the provider dashboard.
2. Check what is queued on sms-tx: bulk texts there are the cause.
3. Pause the bulk send and let the transactional backlog drain.

title: Every email send fails immediately
body:
Applies to: notify-worker.
Use this section when: Every email send fails immediately and the workers log an error for each one, while text messages keep flowing.
Signals: the alert "notify-worker: email send failures above 90%", and log lines such as "NTF-8011 lookup smtp-relay.larkhill.internal failed: SERVFAIL".
Why it happens: The internal resolvers for the notify network could not answer for the larkhill.internal zone. notify-worker could not resolve the name of the SMTP relay, so it never opened a connection.
Steps:
1. Resolve smtp-relay.larkhill.internal from a notify-worker pod.
2. Check the health of both internal resolvers.
3. Restore a resolver or fail over to the secondary pair.

title: payments-gateway: overview and escalation
body: payments-gateway authorises and captures card payments through Meridian Acquiring and writes every movement to the ledger through the ledger connection pooler. The payments on-call owns it. Meridian's operations desk is reached through the acquirer contact sheet. Dashboard: 'Gateway traffic'.

title: Card authorisations declined in bursts
body:
Applies to: payments-gateway.
Use this section when: Card authorisations are declined in bursts while traffic is high, and the same card often succeeds on a retry a minute later.
Signals: the alert "payments-gateway: authorisation decline rate above 8%", and log lines such as "PGW-4012 authorisation declined by upstream code=R29 route=acq-primary".
Why it happens: Meridian Acquiring limits our merchant account to 300 authorisations per second. It answers traffic above that limit with R29 declines, which the gateway logs as PGW-4012.
Steps:
1. Compare authorisations per second on 'Gateway traffic' with the limit of 300 per second.
2. Confirm that the declines carry code R29 and not an issuer decline code.
3. Enable the outbound limiter so that excess requests queue instead of being declined.

title: Every card authorisation fails at once
body:
Applies to: payments-gateway.
Use this section when: Every card authorisation fails within milliseconds and no request reaches the acquirer.
Signals: the alert "payments-gateway: authorisation success rate below 5%", and log lines such as "PGW-5120 handshake with acq-primary failed alert=45".
Why it happens: The client certificate that payments-gateway presents to Meridian Acquiring for mutual TLS passed its expiry date. Meridian rejected the handshake with alert 45, so no authorisation could be sent.
Steps:
1. Read the expiry date of the client certificate in the gateway's secret store.
2. Check that the failures began exactly at the certificate's notAfter time.
3. Deploy the renewed certificate and restart the outbound connectors.

title: Captures time out while authorisations stay fast
body:
Applies to: payments-gateway.
Use this section when: Captures time out after ten seconds while authorisations, which do not write to the ledger, stay fast.
Signals: the alert "payments-gateway: capture latency p99 above 8s", and log lines such as "PGW-3301 no backend slot for ledger write cl_waiting=180".
Why it happens: The ledger connection pooler gives payments-gateway 60 server connections. Transactions held open on the capture path used all 60, and new captures queued for a slot until they timed out.
Steps:
1. Run SHOW POOLS on the ledger pooler: cl_waiting above zero with sv_active at 60 confirms exhaustion.
2. List the transactions from payments-gateway that have been open longest on ledger-db.
3. Stop the job that holds them, then raise the pool limit if traffic alone explains it.
